member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Attributes.ItemAwareAttributeSystem.GetStatAttributes(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Account,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Character)
member.summary: Gets the stat attributes of the character and its account, without duplicates. The attribute system holds exactly one attribute per , so a duplicated definition would fail the construction of the whole system - and with it the login of the character. Duplicates can exist in the stored data, e.g. when a data update added a stat attribute to a character class which already had it, and every character of that class then got the attribute twice. The character's own attribute wins over the one of its account.
member.returns: The distinct stat attributes of the character and its account.

member.summary: Gets the minimum physical base DMG by right hand weapon attribute definition.
member.remarks: Used to isolate RH weapon min damage for double weapon wield logic. On a staff-sword (mixed) or double-staff wield (MG), the LH weapon alone dictates the "attack type": LH: staff; RH: sword/staff => LH physical damage and rise (ene-MG). LH: sword; RH: staff => LH physical damage (str-MG). Other than these, it's a "true" double wield (two one-handed physical weapons) and both weapons' damage attributes count. Summoner can also double weapon wield (stick and book), but books have no damage.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotBuffHandler
member.summary: Lets a bot claim the free buff a dialog NPC offers new players (e.g. the Elf Soldier, which grants defense and damage): when the server has such an NPC configured with a buff the bot qualifies for, it walks up to it and requests the buff like a real player would. The visit reuses the regular player actions (, , ), and while the dialog is open the player state pauses the combat AI - the bot visibly "visits" the NPC.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotBuffHandler.BuffOffersByConfiguration
member.summary: The configured buff offers (which dialog NPC grants which buff), computed once per game configuration: this data does not change at runtime, so re-scanning every configured monster for every bot on every check would be pure waste. Weakly keyed by configuration, so a configuration which gets garbage collected (e.g. a thrown-away test context) is dropped together with its cached offers.

member.summary: The hard limit of characters a single account can hold in the game.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the bot feature is enabled. Disabled by default so that enabling bots is always an explicit, deliberate action.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.ResetBots
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether all bot accounts and characters should be deleted. When set, the feature purges every bot account on the next startup before generating fresh ones, and then automatically clears this flag again. Use it to reset the bot population.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.PurgeBots
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether all bot accounts and characters should be deleted WITHOUT being regenerated. Unlike this also turns off - otherwise the very same pass would generate the population again - so it is the single switch for "I do not want bots on this server anymore". Clears itself afterwards.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.StartAsFreshCharacters
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether newly generated bot characters start as fresh characters, the way a player who just created one does: at level 1 with level-0 starter equipment, no reset history and only the skills its level-1 stats allow. This only affects characters which are generated from now on - an existing bot population keeps its state until it is regenerated ().

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.PresenceRotation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the bot population rotates its presence over the day: fewer bots are online at night, most in the evening, with bots smoothly logging in and out - like a real player base, instead of the same characters being online 24/7.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.MinOnlineSharePercent
member.summary: Gets or sets the share (in percent) of bots which stays online at the quietest time of day. 100 effectively disables the rotation effect.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.NumberOfAccounts
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of bot accounts. Together with this defines the generated bot population, e.g. 10 accounts × 5 characters = 50 bot characters.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.MaxCharactersPerAccount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of characters per bot account. An account can hold at most (5) characters, so this value is clamped on use.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.BotCapacityPercent
member.summary: Gets or sets the share (in percent) of a game server's maximum player count which its bots may occupy. Bots count towards that limit like players do, and a full server turns new clients away - so the rest of the capacity stays reserved for real players, who must never be denied a slot by a bot. The population is split over all configured game servers accordingly (see ); accounts which do not fit stay offline until the servers offer the room for them.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.BotsPayResetCosts
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether bots pay the configured reset costs (zen, reset items) when they reset their character on a server with the reset feature enabled. Off by default: bots don't take part in the player economy the costs are balanced for, so charging them only stalls their progression (a bot can't farm zen for a billion-zen reset the way players trade).

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.JewelStockPerKind
member.summary: Gets or sets how many Jewels of Bless, Soul and Life a bot keeps of each kind. Bots only pick up the jewels they can actually spend on their own gear (see BotJewelHandler) and stop collecting a kind once they hold this many; whatever they carry above it is sold on the next merchant visit. The sensible value depends entirely on the server's drop rates - on a high rate server a bot refills a big stock within hours, so a low limit keeps its backpack usable.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.PotionStockCharges
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of potion charges (per healing and per mana potions) a bot stocks up to at a merchant. Merchants sell potions in stacks of different sizes, so this is the target the bot buys towards, not a stack count.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotConfiguration.ProofOfConceptAccounts
member.summary: Gets or sets a comma separated list of login names of existing accounts to animate as bots. This is an optional extra hook alongside the generated population (see ): every listed account gets a bot driving its first character. These accounts are animated as-is and are not part of the partitioned, capacity-limited population, so leave it empty unless you specifically want to drive existing accounts.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler
member.summary: Lets a bot progress its equipment like a real player: dropped gear is evaluated before pickup (see , used by the offline ), and looted upgrades are periodically equipped; the replaced piece goes into the backpack and is sold on the next shopping trip, so the backpack does not silt up with junk. All moves go through the regular , which enforces the same class- and stat-requirements as for a human player - including which hand a weapon needs (see ).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.UpgradeScoreMargin
member.summary: A candidate must beat the equipped piece by at least this score margin to be worth swapping.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.LastWeaponGroup
member.summary: The highest item group which is a weapon (0 sword, 1 axe, 2 mace, 3 spear, 4 bow, 5 staff).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.ShieldGroup
member.summary: The item group of the shields.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.IsUpgradeFor(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Item)
member.summary: Determines whether the dropped item would be an upgrade over the bot's currently equipped gear, so the pickup handler only collects items worth carrying.
member.param: The bot player which would wear the item.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.TryEquipUpgradesAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer)
member.summary: Scans the bot's backpack for equippable upgrades and puts the best one on; the replaced piece stays in the backpack, where the next shopping trip sells it.
member.param: The bot player whose backpack is scanned.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.TryApplySwapAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.IStorage,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Item,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.EquipSwap)
member.summary: Puts the planned piece on: the gear it replaces goes to the backpack first (an equip only works into a free slot), then the candidate is equipped through the regular . If the engine refuses the equip after all - the requirements are checked against the TOTAL stats, which drop as soon as the old piece with its bonuses comes off - everything moved so far is put back on. Without that rollback the bot ended up with an empty slot, re-equipped the old piece on its next pass and started over: hundreds of swaps per hour, fighting without a weapon half of the time.
member.returns: true if the candidate is now equipped.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.TryPlanSwap(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Item)
member.summary: Plans how the item could be worn: into which slot, and which equipped pieces it would replace. Returns null when the bot would not (or could not) wear it - which is exactly what makes an item worth picking up from the ground, so the pickup handler asks the same question through . Beside the piece in the target slot, a two-handed weapon also replaces whatever blocks the other hand: the engine refuses to equip it otherwise (see ), and a bot which does not plan for that keeps trying (and failing) to put it on forever.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.GetTargetSlots(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.Items.ItemDefinition)
member.summary: The slots the bot considers for this piece: a weapon only goes into the main hand and a shield only into the off-hand - a bot filling its off-hand with a second (junk) weapon it happens to be qualified for is neither useful nor a sight any real character offers. Everything else may go into any of its qualified slots (rings have two).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.IsWearableCandidate(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.Items.ItemDefinition,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.CharacterClass)
member.summary: Whether the item is gear this bot would wear at all: an equippable, class-qualified piece which - if it is a weapon - matches the fighting style of the bot's build (an elf only considers bows, a caster only staves), so bots don't fill their hands with random qualified junk like a Small Axe.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.Score(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Item)
member.summary: A rough, monotonic quality score of an equippable item: the definition's drop level tracks the gear tier, the item level its upgrades, and excellent/ancient options add their extra worth.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.EquipSwap
member.summary: A planned equip: the slot the candidate goes into, and the equipped pieces which have to come off for it (the gear in the target slot, plus the other hand's item when a two-handed weapon needs it).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotEquipmentHandler.EquipSwap.#ctor(System.Byte,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Item})
member.summary: A planned equip: the slot the candidate goes into, and the equipped pieces which have to come off for it (the gear in the target slot, plus the other hand's item when a two-handed weapon needs it).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn._states
member.summary: The state of the feature, per game server: the plugin instance is shared by all game servers of the process, while is called by each of them separately. One shared state would mean the server whose timer fires first animates the whole population (which is how the bots used to end up on a single server), and the other servers doing nothing at all.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.StartupPhase
member.summary: The phase of a game server's single startup pass. The periodic task timer fires every second WITHOUT awaiting the previous invocation, so during the minutes-long generation/spawn further ticks arrive concurrently - they must neither re-enter the startup nor run the maintenance (e.g. the presence rotation) against a half-spawned population.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.RunMaintenanceAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameContext,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.ServerState)
member.summary: Runs the periodic post-spawn maintenance: the presence rotation (one bot in or out per pass, so the population ebbs and flows smoothly over the day) and an hourly party re-formation which groups bots that lost or never had a party (e.g. after rotating back in).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.RestartFaultedBotsAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameContext,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.ServerState,Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger)
member.summary: Restarts bots whose AI keeps throwing (see ). The engine's attribute system is not thread-safe, and a lost race can corrupt a character's attribute graph for good: the bot stops playing and every following tick throws the same exception, up to a flood of them per second. A fresh login rebuilds the graph and heals it - the same thing a player would do, and the only cure available from outside the engine. Runs from the maintenance pass, which is the only place allowed to restart a bot.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.EvolveDueMastersAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameContext,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.ServerState,Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger)
member.summary: Evolves bots which reached the game's maximum level into their master class (see for the rules, including the iron rule of reset servers). Runs from the maintenance pass - outside the bot's own AI tick - because the evolved bot is restarted right away (see ), which must not happen from within one of its own timer callbacks.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.RestartEvolvedBotAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameContext,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotFeaturePlugIn.ServerState,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer,Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger)
member.summary: Gives the freshly evolved bot the "relog" it needs: the master class's base attributes (master experience rate, master points per level) and the master level stat are only mounted when a character enters the world (see ).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator
member.summary: Generates and maintains the persistent population of bot accounts and their characters.
member.remarks: Accounts are flagged with so they can be reliably reloaded on startup (instead of being regenerated) and purged on request. The account login names follow a deterministic, internal scheme () which is never shown to other players; the player-visible character names are realistic and unique (see ). Generation is idempotent: only the missing accounts are created, so it is safe to run on every start.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.BotPasswordWorkFactor
member.summary: BCrypt work factor for a bot account's password. The password is a random which is discarded immediately and never used to log in - a bot is a connection-less OfflinePlayer, so no client ever authenticates against it. A minimal factor is therefore safe (a 128-bit random secret is infeasible to brute-force regardless of the factor) and keeps generating a large population from becoming a multi-minute BCrypt bottleneck, while still storing a valid BCrypt hash. The default factor is kept for real accounts.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.BotInventoryExtensions
member.summary: Number of inventory extensions (each 4 rows of 8 slots) a bot gets, so loot does not clog its backpack.

member.summary: Builds a shuffled queue of character classes with even quotas across , so the generated population is balanced instead of relying on the variance of independent random draws. The order is randomized so accounts do not get a predictable class pattern.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.DistributeStatPoints(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Character,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.CharacterClass,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Spends the character's level-up points, so a high-level bot actually has high-level stats. Without this a generated level-80 bot would fight with level-1 base stats (tiny health and damage) and die instantly. The split follows the class build in - the same split the bot keeps using for points it earns at runtime - and respects each stat's configured maximum (fun servers) as well as the bot's personal vitality target on reset-meta servers.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.CalculateLevelUpPoints(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.CharacterClass,System.Int32,System.Int32,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Resets.ResetConfiguration)
member.summary: Calculates the level-up points a character with the given reset history would have available, so a seeded bot invests the same total a player of that history would: the points granted by the resets themselves (looped through , so tiers, multipliers and the replace/add mode of the server's configuration all apply) plus the points earned by leveling. With the level points of the finished cycles were invested and wiped again at each reset, so only the current cycle's count; without it every cycle's investment survived and still counts.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.CollectBotLoginNamesAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Persistence.IPlayerContext,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Collects the login names of all bot accounts, ordered by login name.
member.returns: The login names of the bot accounts.
member.remarks: Collected first, deleted afterwards: the paging query orders by login name, so deleting while paging would shift the accounts which are not visited yet into the pages already passed.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.TryDeleteBotAccountAsync(System.String,MUnique.OpenMU.Persistence.IPlayerContext,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Tries to delete a single bot account with its characters, item storages, and items.
member.param: The login name of the bot account.
member.returns: The outcome of the deletion.
member.remarks: One bad account returns instead of aborting the whole purge; the caller fails the purge as a whole, so the flags stay set and it gets retried instead of switching the feature off with the bot accounts still in the database. Cancellation is never swallowed.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotGenerator.LearnClassSkills(MUnique.OpenMU.Persistence.IPlayerContext,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Entities.Character,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.CharacterClass,System.Int32)
member.summary: Teaches the character the class skills appropriate to its level and stats - attack skills as well as the class's own buffs and heals (e.g. elf Heal/Greater Defense/Greater Damage). Only skills the class is qualified for are ever learned, gated by the skills' real learn requirements from the game configuration (total energy, leadership, character level, ...) evaluated against the stats the bot was just given - exactly the requirements a human player has to meet for the same skill. Item-bound skills follow the backfill rules (see ): orb/scroll skills only when their granting item is obtainable, so a bot cannot learn a scroll before the monster level where it starts to drop - and never when the skill comes from worn equipment or a pet, which the server grants temporarily on equip instead.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotJewelHandler
member.summary: Lets a bot invest its looted jewels into its own gear like a real player would: after a shopping trip (a rare, safe moment in town), it takes a piece of equipment off, applies a Jewel of Bless, Soul or Life through the regular - the same validations, success rates and failure penalties as for a human - and puts the piece back on. The policy mirrors common player behavior: Bless (always succeeds) pushes the weakest equipped piece towards +6, whether it has luck or not; Soul (50%, +25% with luck; a failure at +6 drops the item to +5, from +7 on it resets it to +0) is only risked with a spare in stock, on plain items only at +6 and up to +9 only on lucky ones; Life (50%, removes the option on failure) is used sparingly on already upgraded gear. Only a couple of jewels are spent per trip, so the upgrades trickle in over many visits like for a player instead of the whole hoard being burned at once.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotJewelHandler.UsableJewels
member.summary: The jewels a bot has a use for: it upgrades its own gear with them (see the policy above). Everything else - Chaos, Creation, Guardian, Gemstone, Harmony, the refine stones - is only spendable by trading or crafting, which a bot does neither of.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotJewelHandler.UnusableJewels
member.summary: Jewels a bot may still be carrying from before but can never spend: it neither trades nor crafts. They are not picked up anymore, so this is about clearing out what is already in the backpack.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotJewelHandler.MaxBlessPerTrip
member.summary: Jewels of Bless per shopping trip. Each kind has its OWN budget on purpose: with one shared budget the Bless rule - which has a target whenever any equipped piece is below +6, and a swapped in piece arrives at the level it dropped with - consumed every use, every trip, and the Soul and Life rules below were never reached at all.

member.summary: Safety net for the planning loop; the per-kind budgets are the real limit.

member.summary: Without luck a Soul is only risked at +6, where a failure merely drops the item to +5 (a Bless restores that): from +7 on, a failed Soul resets the item to +0 (ResetToLevel0WhenFailMinLevel in SoulJewelConsumeHandlerPlugIn), and at the base 50% success rate that gamble wipes gear more often than not.

member.summary: With luck (+25% success) the Soul may be risked up to +8, so lucky items can reach the jewel ceiling of +9 (MaximumLevel in SoulJewelConsumeHandlerPlugIn).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotManager
member.summary: Manages the lifecycle of server-side bots.
member.remarks: A bot reuses the connection-less together with its MU Helper AI, but is spawned in a fully standalone way: the account is loaded fresh in the bot's own persistence context (see ), so there is no cross-context attach of entities owned by another player - which is the root cause of the known data-corruption issue of the /offlevel handover. Because each bot drives a distinct character in its own context, several bots can animate different characters of the same account at once (the shared account row is only attached, never modified).

member.summary: Stops the given bot like a regular logout and immediately brings the same character back online - the ghost equivalent of a player relogging. Used after the master evolution: the master class's base attributes (master experience rate, master points per level) and the master level stat are only mounted when the character enters the world, so the class change must be followed by a fresh world entry before master experience can flow.
member.returns: true if the bot came back online.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotManager.FormPartiesAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.IGameContext)
member.summary: Groups a share of the active bots into small hunting parties of level-wise similar characters, like real players do: the party members follow their leader (see the follow logic in ), the elf heals the group, buffs are shared and the party experience bonus applies. The rest of the bots keep hunting solo, so the population stays varied.
member.param: The game context (provides the party manager).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotManager.StopAndDisposeAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Stops the bot like a regular logout (which saves its progress) and releases its resources. A stopped-but-not-disposed player keeps its persistence context - and with it the whole tracked account graph - alive; with the presence rotation stopping bots around the clock, that adds up to a leak. Mirrors the teardown of the : the removal from the game context normally happens through the disconnect event, and when the stop threw before it could raise that event, the disposal removes the bot as its own safety net (see ).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotManager.RemoveAndDisposeAsync(System.String,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer)
member.summary: Drops a bot which never got as far as playing. It was already added to the game context if its initialization failed after was reached, and it is never disconnected on this path - the disposal takes it out of the player list (see ).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler
member.summary: Handles the third-generation ("master") stage of a bot's career: the evolution into the master class at the game's maximum level - the same class assignment the level-400 master quests perform for a human player - and the investment of the master points earned per master level, through the regular with all its validations.
member.remarks: On servers with the reset feature the evolution follows one iron rule: a bot only becomes a master when no reset can ever follow, i.e. the configured reset limit is exhausted. While resets remain - or when no limit is configured at all, so resetting forever is the endgame - the bot keeps resetting and never masters, like the players of such servers. Without the reset feature it evolves as soon as it reaches the maximum level. The master class's base attributes (master experience rate, master points per level) and the master level stat are only mounted into the attribute system when the character enters the world, so the caller must restart the bot after the evolution (see BotManager.RestartBotAsync) - the ghost equivalent of a player relogging; master experience only flows after that fresh world entry.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.RankUnlockLevel
member.summary: A master skill unlocks the next rank of its root (and satisfies "required skill" links) at this level, see .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.SwordGroup
member.summary: The item groups of the weapons a master bonus can be tied to (see ).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.MaceGroup
member.summary: The item group of the maces - the scepters live here as well.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.SpearGroup
member.summary: The item group of the spears.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.BowGroup
member.summary: The item group of the bows and crossbows.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.StaffGroup
member.summary: The item group of the staffs - the sticks and books live here as well.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.IsMasterEvolutionDue(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Determines whether the bot is due for its master evolution: it has a master class to evolve into, stands at the game's maximum level, and - on reset servers - exhausted the reset limit (see the remarks of for the rationale).
member.returns: True, if the bot should evolve into its master class now.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.TryEvolveAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer)
member.summary: Evolves the bot into its master class when due. The caller must restart the bot afterwards (see the remarks of ).
member.returns: True, if the evolution was performed.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.HasMasterPointsToSpend(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Determines whether the bot is a master with points to invest - the cheap per-tick guard for queueing .
member.returns: True, if there are master points to spend.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.TrySpendMasterPointsAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer)
member.summary: Invests the bot's available master points (earned one per master level) into its master skill tree through the regular . Learning a skill mutates the skill list, so this must run inside the bot's AI tick - queue it via (see the call site in BotNavigator); with no points available it is a cheap no-op.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.PickNextMasterSkill(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Picks the master skill the bot invests its next point into, or null when nothing is eligible. The policy fills the tree like a player: first push a started skill to the rank-unlock level of 10, then learn a new eligible skill - preferring "useful" ones, i.e. passives boosting a stat or strengtheners of a skill the bot actually has - and finally pump the learned skills towards their maximum. Deterministic, so a bot builds the same tree across sessions. Pure decision logic - exposed for unit tests.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.CanLearn(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.Skill,System.Int32)
member.summary: Mirrors the private requisition checks of (minimum points, previous rank of the same root at 10+, required skills), so the picker only proposes skills the action will accept. A mismatch is harmless: the action refuses and the spend loop stops.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.IsUsefulPick(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.Skill,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.ISkillList)
member.summary: A pick is "useful" when it demonstrably does something for this bot: a passive boosting a stat, or a strengthener/mastery of a skill the bot actually has in its list. A passive tied to a WEAPON type the bot does not fight with is not (a bow strengthener does nothing for a bot swinging a sword), and neither is one which only applies against other PLAYERS: a bot spends its life hunting monsters, and it may not even attack a player unless attacked first (see ). Both get filled last, after everything which actually helps.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.IsPvpOnlyBonus(MUnique.OpenMU.AttributeSystem.AttributeDefinition)
member.summary: Whether the master bonus only ever applies in a fight against another player, which is not what a bot's points are for.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.WeaponGroupOfBonus(MUnique.OpenMU.AttributeSystem.AttributeDefinition)
member.summary: The item group of the weapon a master bonus attribute belongs to, or null when the bonus helps regardless of the weapon (health, defense, an attack rate, ...). The item groups come from the item data: scepters live in the mace group, the Rage Fighter's gloves in the sword group, and sticks and books next to the staffs.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMasterHandler.CarriesWeaponOfGroup(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,System.Byte)
member.summary: Whether the bot fights with a weapon of this item group - what it carries right now, and what its build makes it pick up in the future (see ), so a bot which is momentarily unarmed does not start collecting bonuses for the wrong weapon.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMiniGameHandler
member.summary: Lets server-side bots take part in the mini game events (Blood Castle, Devil Square, Chaos Castle) - but only ever in the wake of a human: when a real player who leads a party with bots enters an event with their own ticket, the party's bots follow them in. Bots never enter on their own, and they don't need tickets - the leader's entry is what legitimizes the visit. Each bot is checked against the same entry rules a player faces (the event level bracket, the master class requirement, the player killer restriction); a bot which does not qualify says goodbye and leaves the party to go back to its own hunting life, like a player who cannot join the run. Inside, the bot's routine switches to the event mode of the ; death and the event's end need no special handling, because the engine respawns a dead bot at the map's safezone (exactly like a player, which removes it from the event) and the event itself warps the remaining participants out when it ends.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMiniGameHandler.SnapshotPartyBots(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Takes the snapshot of the bots which would follow the given player into a mini game. Must be called BEFORE the player actually enters: entering an event which disallows parties (Chaos Castle) kicks the entering player out of its party, and with it the knowledge of who was going to follow.
member.param: The player about to enter a mini game.
member.returns: The party bots to bring along; empty when the player is a bot itself, has no party or is not its master.

member.summary: Brings the party bots of a player who just successfully entered a mini game along into it. Each bot's entry is queued into its own MuHelper tick (see ), because warping and effect-clearing mutate the bot's state.
member.param: The party leader who entered the mini game.
The snapshot taken by before the entry.
The definition of the entered mini game.
The mini game instance the leader entered.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMiniGameHandler.IsEligible(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.MiniGameDefinition,System.String@)
member.summary: Determines whether the bot passes the same entry restrictions EnterMiniGameAction checks for a player: the event's character level bracket, the master class requirement and the player killer restriction. Pure decision logic - exposed for unit tests.
member.param: The bot which wants to follow its leader in.
The human-readable reason when the bot does not qualify.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings
member.summary: Default MU Helper settings used to drive a bot's combat AI. A bot never sends a client-side MU Helper configuration, so without this the player would fall back to a hunting range of a single tile (see ). These defaults make the bot hunt nearby monsters, pick up the valuable drops and use potions, while staying close to its spawn origin.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.ReturnToOriginalPosition
member.remarks: Disabled for bots: the is the sole driver of travel between hunting grounds, so the offline movement handler must not try to walk the bot back to its origin in parallel.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.RepairItem
member.remarks: Disabled on purpose: offline auto-repair has no NPC discount and drains Zen at an increased rate. Bots should not burn their balance on repairs during the proof of concept.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.UseSelfDefense
member.remarks: Bots fight back when a player attacks them (see ).

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.AutoAcceptAnyone
member.remarks: Bots accept party invitations from any player, like a friendly stranger would - within the safeguards applied by (level gap, not while busy, limited time).

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.AutoSelectBestSkill
member.remarks: Enabled for bots: they have no client-side skill configuration, so the combat AI auto-selects the strongest learned attack skill the character can currently afford. Combined with the level-gated skills granted at generation (see ), this makes bots cast class- and level-appropriate magic/skills instead of only swinging their weapon.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.AutoSelectBuffs
member.remarks: Bots keep their class's learned buffs up automatically (e.g. elf Greater Defense/Greater Damage).

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.UseManaPotion
member.remarks: Casters drink mana potions, so they keep casting instead of degrading to weak melee.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.OnlyHuntSafeMonsters
member.remarks: Bots only engage monsters they can handle (the navigator's safe-monster cap). Without this, a bot travelling through hostile territory picks fights with monsters far above its level and dies.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotMuHelperSettings.PickUpgradeItems
member.remarks: Bots evaluate dropped gear and pick up upgrades for their own class (see ).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNameGenerator
member.summary: Generates pronounceable, realistic-looking character names for bots.
member.remarks: Names are built procedurally from syllables so the generator scales to thousands of unique names while still looking like names a real player might pick. Every generated name satisfies the default character name rules (3-10 alphanumeric characters), so bots blend in with players; the bot nature is tracked by , never by the name.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNameGenerator.GenerateUniqueAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Persistence.IPlayerContext,System.Collections.Generic.ISet{System.String},System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Generates a name which is not yet used, neither within this run nor in the database.
member.param: The context used to check name availability.
The set of names already handed out in this run; the returned name is added to it.
member.returns: A unique, valid character name.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator
member.summary: Drives a bot's high-level navigation. It picks a hunting ground that suits the bot's level from the monster spawn areas of the current map and points the bot's at it. The existing offline movement handler then walks the bot there (using the server pathfinder) and the combat handler hunts locally - so a bot which spawns in town finds its own way to the monsters.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.WarpImprovementMargin
member.summary: A bot only warps to another map if it offers safe monsters at least this many levels stronger. Sized as a hysteresis band: the safety verdict for a borderline monster flips when the bot's defense changes with its buffs, and a small margin let two maps leapfrog each other on every re-evaluation - the bot ping-ponged between them on warp cooldown.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MinWarpLevel
member.summary: Below this level a bot never warps: it stays on its class starting map (e.g. elves in Noria, summoners in Elvenland), so the newbie maps stay populated instead of everyone drifting to one map.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BandWidth
member.summary: Width of the level band of areas we randomize between, so bots don't all stack on one spot.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HuntingRange
member.summary: Range (tiles) around the origin that counts as "at the hunting ground".

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ProximityFalloff
member.summary: Distance (tiles) at which a hunting ground counts as half as attractive as one the bot is standing on. See .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.GroundScatterSpan
member.summary: Width (tiles) of the box a hunting ground point is sampled from when the spawn area itself is smaller. See .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ShoppingSpread
member.summary: Share of the shopping cooldown the next trip is spread over, so that bots which shopped together don't come back together. See .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BuffSpread
member.summary: Share of the buff check interval the next check is spread over, so bots don't all walk to the buff NPC at once. See .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MonsterSeekRadius
member.summary: How far the bot looks for an actual live monster to home in on. MU spawn areas span most of the map (e.g. Lorencia's are ~86x233 / ~105x68 tiles) with only a few dozen monsters each, so their monsters sit ~20 tiles apart. Walking to a random tile inside such an area almost never lands within the 6-tile combat range of a real monster - the bot arrives, finds nothing to fight, and wanders off. So once the bot is anywhere in the region it scans this radius for the nearest live monster and heads straight for it. Kept modest so the per-tick area-of-interest scan stays cheap even with hundreds of bots.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HealPotionGroup
member.summary: Item group of potions (healing and mana potions share group 14).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HealPotionNumber
member.summary: Item number of the Large Healing Potion within .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ManaPotionNumber
member.summary: Item number of the Large Mana Potion within .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EmergencyPotionCharges
member.summary: How many charges an emergency refill stocks up (the potion item's Durability holds the remaining count; one is spent per heal). Spread over as many item stacks as the definition's stack size needs: a Large Healing Potion holds three charges per stack, so a bot handed a single 255-charge "potion" carried an item the game cannot produce - its stack never looked low again (the shopping loop for that potion kind went dead), and stacking it with a bought one underflowed the count.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HealPotionRefillBelow
member.summary: Emergency refill threshold: normally the bot restocks potions by BUYING them at a merchant (see , triggered well above this level); only when a stack still runs this low (e.g. no Zen, merchant unreachable) is it topped up out of thin air as a last resort, so the bot never dies over an empty bottle.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.StepsPerHop
member.summary: Number of path steps to issue per travel hop. Short hops let the bot stop and fight between hops.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.PathReuseTolerance
member.summary: How far the travel destination may drift (e.g. a roaming monster the bot homes in on) before the cached route is re-planned. Re-planning a whole-map A* every tick just to consume three steps starved the pathfinder pool once dozens of bots traveled at the same time.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MerchantTalkRange
member.summary: How close (tiles) the bot must be to the merchant to trade.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TravelStopRange
member.summary: If a monster is within this range the bot stops traveling and lets the combat handler engage. MUST equal the combat hunting range: the combat handler only ever targets monsters within of the bot, so stopping for anything further away would hand control to the combat handler for a monster it never fights - the bot would freeze in place (stop travelling, but find nothing to attack) until the monster happened to wander off.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TravelSearchLimit
member.summary: Search limit for the travel pathfinder, generous enough for a full cross-map route.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TravelHeuristicWeight
member.summary: Heuristic weight while traveling: high enough to make the A* search greedy and cheap over long routes.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.FollowDistance
member.summary: Follow trigger for mini-game events: a participant further than this (tiles) from its leader walks back. Open-world party formation uses instead.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.PartyRegroupDistance
member.summary: Open-world formation radius: with nothing to fight around the leader, a follower closes back in to within this distance (tiles). Deliberately tighter than , so the party stacks up when idle; the regroup walk itself is gated on "no fightable monster near the leader" (see ), so combat drift out to hunting range never triggers a yank-back mid-fight.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.DeathSiteAvoidanceRange
member.summary: Hunting grounds closer than this (tiles) to a recent death site are avoided after the same player killed the bot repeatedly (see ), so the bot farms somewhere else instead of walking back into the same lost fight.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BestCandidateShare
member.summary: Share of the picks the best ranked map takes when the bot chooses where to hunt (see ); the runners-up split what is left, on the same terms. Below a half on purpose: at a half the fourth map of a level band and everything behind it share a few percent between them, which left Karutan, Icarus and Kanturu with three or four bots each while the top map held a hundred. The bot still prefers the best ground - every candidate it draws from is already a step up from where it stands - it just does not treat the runner-up as worthless.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.WarpAction
member.summary: The game's own warp action, so a bot travels on exactly a player's terms - fare included.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.WalkableSpawnGateCache
member.summary: Cache of which maps' safezone spawn gates have a walkable tile, so a bot may safely be sent there. Keyed by the resolved safezone map's id, not its number: map numbers are not unique - the Devil Squares share number 9, and a server can host several game configurations whose maps carry the same numbers over different terrain. See .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EquipCheckInterval
member.summary: How often the bot checks its backpack for equippable upgrades.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ShoppingCheckInterval
member.summary: How often the bot considers whether it needs a shopping trip.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ShoppingCooldown
member.summary: Cooldown after a shopping trip before considering the next one.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BuffCheckInterval
member.summary: How often the bot re-evaluates whether it should claim a buff NPC's free buff: a level-eligible bot could claim it right away, so the check re-fires quickly while the buff has not yet been applied.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BuffCooldown
member.summary: Cooldown after a buff trip before considering the next one, so bots which just got the buff (and level-eligible ones which could not claim it) don't re-walk to the NPC every check interval.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.WarpCooldown
member.summary: Minimum time between two cross-map warps, so a bot does not bounce between maps (a real player does not hop maps every minute either).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BarrenMapDuration
member.summary: How long a bot may go without landing a single hit before it treats its map as barren and steps down (see ). Long enough that a walk across a map, a merchant trip or a quiet stretch between spawns does not count as one.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.FollowWarpCooldown
member.summary: Cooldown for following the party leader to another map (shorter, so the group regroups quickly).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.LeaderSettleTime
member.summary: How long the party leader has to stay on a map before its bots follow him there. A leader who is only passing through (a town trip for supplies, a gate on the way somewhere) must not drag his whole party across the world and back - real party members wait to see where he settles, too.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MinResetDelay
member.summary: Bounds of the random delay between becoming eligible for a character reset and performing it. A real player finishes the fight, walks to town, maybe trades first - and 250 bots resetting the very second they hit the required level would be an obvious give-away (and a thundering herd of simultaneous re-gearing). The delay is rolled per bot when it becomes eligible.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MaxResetDelay
member.summary: Upper bound of the random reset delay, see .

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.StuckTimeout
member.summary: If the bot's position has not changed for this long, it is considered stuck (a wedged walk, or a monster it can't reach). The navigator then forces a fresh destination, so the bot gets going again.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.StuckWithMonstersTimeout
member.summary: Stuck timeout when huntable monsters are nearby: much longer, because a bot standing still while monsters are around is usually just fighting them from one tile. It still eventually fires, which breaks the rare deadlock of a monster that is in range but cannot be attacked or reached.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TravelPathFinderPoolSize
member.summary: A pool of full-map pathfinders for long-distance travel. The pooled (scoped) pathfinder rejects start/end further apart than ~16 tiles, so travel uses a which resolves routes across the whole map. A pathfinder is not safe for concurrent use, so we keep a small pool and hand one out per call: several bots can plan routes in parallel (a single shared instance serialized every bot and starved navigation once the population reached the hundreds), while the pool size caps how many CPU cores whole-map searches may occupy at once.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator._buffTarget
member.summary: Target position of the current buff trip, or null, if there is none.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator._nextBuffCheckUtc
member.summary: When the bot considers a buff trip again. Like the shopping check, the first one is spread over the cooldown (not "now"), so bots don't all march to the Elf Soldier at once.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator._nextShoppingCheckUtc
member.summary: When this bot looks at its supplies again. Bots come up with the server, so starting them all at "now" sent the whole population to the same merchant in the same minute - and since the cooldown was the same for everyone, nothing ever broke that herd apart again. The first check is therefore spread over the cooldown, and every following one is spread around it.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.#ctor(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.Start
member.summary: Starts the periodic navigation evaluation. The start delay is jittered per bot, so hundreds of navigators do not all fire on the same second boundary (smoother load, less robotic synchrony).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.GroundWeight(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.MonsterSpawnArea,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point)
member.summary: Rates a spawn area as a hunting ground for a bot standing at the given point.
member.param: The point the bot measures from.
member.returns: The relative weight of the area.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HasWalkableSpawnGate(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition)
member.summary: Whether a bot may safely be sent to the map: the safezone spawn gate it would be recovered to has at least one walkable tile. A warp which lands a bot on a blocked tile is recovered by , and for a connection-less bot that recovery runs inline (see ) - so a spawn gate with no walkable tile at all used to recurse until the stack overflowed. The player's map transitions now bound that recovery, so this filter is no longer what keeps the server alive; it keeps the bot from picking a map it cannot stand in and being bounced straight back out of it.
member.param: The map the bot considers warping to.
member.returns: True, if the map's resolved safezone spawn gate has a walkable tile.
member.remarks: The verdict is cached for the lifetime of the process, keyed by the resolved safezone map - terrain is static configuration, so it is parsed once and shared by every bot. Terrain edited through the admin panel therefore needs a server restart to be taken into account. Only maps whose spawn gate has *zero* walkable tiles are excluded. A gate with a few walkable tiles can still, under PlaceAtGateAsync's single random roll, miss and recover to town - a quality glitch, not a crash, accepted by design.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HasWalkableSpawnGateCore(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition)
member.summary: The uncached terrain check behind , on an already resolved safezone map.
member.returns: True, if the map's spawn gate has a walkable tile.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.NextShoppingCheckUtc
member.summary: Manhattan distance between the center of the spawn area and the given point.
Returns the time of the next supply check, spread around so that bots which just shopped together don't queue up at the merchant together again.
member.returns: The time of the next supply check.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.NextBuffCheckUtc
member.summary: Returns the time of the next buff consideration, spread around so that bots which just went to the buff NPC together don't line up there again.
member.returns: The time of the next buff consideration.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.PickByRank(System.Int32)
member.summary: Picks an index into a list ranked best-first, each rank taking of what the ranks before it left over. Deliberately not a uniform draw - a bot should prefer the best ground it can hunt, just not to the exclusion of everything else.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryShoppingAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Drives a shopping trip: when the backpack fills up or potions run low, the bot heads to a town merchant (warping to the map's safezone first when out in the field, like using a town portal), walks up to it and trades - selling junk loot and restocking potions with Zen.
member.returns: True, if the shopping trip consumed this tick.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TradeAndUpgradeAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point)
member.summary: The trade at the merchant, as it runs inside the MU Helper tick: sell the junk, restock the potions and - still standing safely at the shop with the dialog closed - spend a few of the looted jewels on the own gear, the player-like moment for it (see ).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryBuffTripAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Drives a buff trip: when the server has a dialog NPC offering a buff the bot qualifies for (the Elf Soldier grants fresh characters a defense and a damage buff, but exists only in Season Six data), the bot heads to it - warping to the map's safezone first when out in the field, like using a town portal - walks up to it and claims the buff like a real player would. Without data to configure the NPC the check simply never fires, so this is a no-op on earlier seasons.
member.param: Indicates whether the bot currently is in the safezone of the map.
The token which aborts the travel wait on shutdown.
member.returns: True, if the buff trip consumed this tick.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ClaimBuffAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point)
member.summary: Claims the buff at the buff NPC, as it runs inside the MU Helper tick: open the dialog, request the buff, close the dialog - the player-like visit, see .
member.param: The position of the buff NPC.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryRevengeMarchAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Marches the bot back to the place of its death while revenge is armed (see ). The single attempt is spent as soon as the bot arrives or runs into its killer on the way - no extra combat logic is needed here, because the re-armed aggressor memory already keeps the combat handler prioritizing the killer, struck only when legal (see ). Monsters along the route do not stop the march (self-defense still engages ones right next to the bot); a bot that stopped to farm would never arrive within the revenge time.
member.param: The token which aborts the travel wait on shutdown.
member.returns: True, if the revenge march consumed this tick.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EvaluateInsideMiniGameAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: The bot's routine while it takes part in a mini-game event (Blood Castle, Devil Square, Chaos Castle): fight whatever the event throws at it, keep up with the party leader on the way through the course, and close in on the action when it moved away - nothing else. Death and the event's end need no handling here: the engine respawns a dead bot at the map's safezone like a player (which removes it from the event), and the event warps the remaining participants out when it ends.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.IsEventTarget(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.IAttackable)
member.summary: Whether the object is something this bot would fight inside a mini-game event. Unlike in the open world, there is no safe-level filtering - the event's level bracket already matched the bot, and the event dictates the opposition. Players count as targets only where the event allows player killing (Chaos Castle, see ).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryFindNearestEventTargetGround(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point@)
member.summary: Finds the spot of a nearby opponent inside a mini-game event, mirroring (random among the two nearest, so many bots don't dogpile the same target).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.GetPartyLeaderToFollow
member.summary: Gets the party leader this bot should follow, or null if the bot is solo, is the leader itself, or the leader is currently not followable (dead, no map, or inside another mini-game instance - following into an event goes through the regular entry of , never through a warp).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryFollowLeaderAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Follows the party leader across maps: warps to the leader's map when the leader warped away and settled there. Same-map spacing is NOT handled here - it is owned by , which gates the regroup walk on "nothing to fight", so a follower engaged at hunting range is never yanked back mid-fight.
member.returns: True, if cross-map following consumed this tick; false, if on the same map (follower hunting runs next).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EvaluateFollowerHuntingAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,System.Boolean,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Hunts around the party leader on the same map: monsters within hunting range (, mirroring the follower's effective combat range of ) of the leader are fought via the combat handler (tethered through , which is also set where the origin is decided so it holds on walking ticks), and only with nothing fightable near the leader does the bot close back in to within . Followers never pick independent hunting grounds - the leader decides where the party hunts.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.HasLeaderSettled(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Whether the leader has been on his current map long enough () for the bot to follow him there. Tracks the leader's map per bot, so each follower makes the call on its own.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryResetCharacterAsync
member.summary: Performs the bot's character reset once it is due (reset feature enabled, required level reached, reset limit not exhausted). The reset is not executed the moment the bot becomes eligible: a random grace delay (..) is rolled first, during which the bot hunts on normally. After the reset, the navigation state is cleared, so the bot starts its next cycle fresh - re-investing its points (queued by the reset handler) and heading for a hunting ground that suits it again.
member.returns: True, if a reset was performed.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryWarpToBetterMapAsync
member.summary: Warps to the map that offers the strongest monsters this bot can still safely handle, so it earns the best experience without being slaughtered. It arrives at the destination safezone and walks out to a hunting ground like a real player.
member.returns: True, if a warp was performed.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TravelTowardAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Walks the next stretch towards the destination. A full route is resolved with a heuristic search (so it goes around walls and out of the town gate) and the first steps are issued; the remainder is recomputed from the new position on the next tick. The safe zone is allowed in the path so the bot can leave town.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.WalkCachedStepsAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point)
member.summary: Issues the next few steps of the cached route (short hops, so the bot can stop and fight between them) and advances the route cursor.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.PickGroundAndTravelAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Picks a hunting ground and starts walking to it. If the chosen ground turns out to be unreachable, the destination is dropped, so the next call (next tick) simply picks another one.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EnsurePotionsAsync
member.summary: Ensures the bot keeps a stack of healing and a stack of mana potions in its inventory. Creates the stacks the first time (covering bots generated before they were granted) and refills them once they run low, so the bot never goes without a way to heal or to keep casting.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.EnsureAmmunitionAsync
member.summary: Keeps an archer's ammunition topped up. With the starter bow the offline attack path does not consume arrows, but an upgraded bow can carry an ammunition consumption rate - without this the bot would eventually shoot its quiver empty and its bow skills would stop working.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryFindNearestMonsterGround(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point@)
member.summary: Finds the position of the nearest live, attackable monster within that the bot can safely fight, so the bot heads straight for a real monster instead of a random tile in a huge spawn area. Returns false when none are loaded nearby (or all are above the safe level cap), in which case the caller falls back to coarse spawn-area travel / warping to relocate.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryPersistCurrentMapAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition)
member.summary: Re-resolves the warp destination map through the bot's own persistence context and assigns that instance to the character. The warp itself assigns the GLOBAL configuration instance, which the bot's context does not track - the CurrentMapId foreign key silently never got saved, so a restarted bot always woke up on its home map and warped all over again (warp burst on restart).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.GetBotLevel
member.summary: The bot's reset-aware effective level (see ), used for hunting decisions (which monsters pay off). Map ACCESS is deliberately not decided by this - the game gates warps by the plain character level (see ), and the bots must obey the same rule.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryGetLegalWarp(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.WarpInfo@)
member.summary: Gets the gate through which the bot may legally warp to the given map, exactly like a player using the in-game warp window: the map must have an entry in the server's warp list whose level requirement (class-reduced, see ) is met by the bot's PLAIN character level. The reset-aware effective level intentionally plays no role here - a freshly reset veteran cannot warp to high maps either, no matter its strength.
member.param: The warp info, if a legal entry exists.
member.returns: True, if the bot may warp to the map.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.CanAffordWarp(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.WarpInfo)
member.summary: Whether the bot can pay the warp's fare. A bot travels on the same terms as a player - it pays what the warp costs - so a map it cannot afford is not offered to it in the first place, rather than chosen and then refused by .

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryGetHomeEscapeGate(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.ExitGate@,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Gets the escape gate to the bot's class hometown, for when it must leave its current map but is below every warp requirement (e.g. a freshly reset veteran) - the equivalent of a town scroll.
member.param: The level of the strongest safe monster there (informational).
member.returns: True, if the bot has a home map it is not already on.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.MasterExperienceFloor
member.summary: The lowest monster level that still earns this bot anything: a master-class character at the game's maximum level gains master experience only from monsters of at least GameConfiguration.MinimumMonsterLevelForMasterExperience (the experience path grants it nothing at all below that) and no regular experience either, because it is at the maximum level already. Hunting below that floor is therefore not the safe choice for a mastered bot, it is a dead end - so the map and hunting ground choice look above the floor first. 0 for every other bot, which hunts by safety alone.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.BestSafeLevel(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition,System.Int32)
member.summary: The level of the strongest monster on the map which this bot can safely fight (judged by the monster's real damage against the bot's defense and health, see ); 0 if the map has none. The level of the safe monsters remains the measure of a map's experience value when comparing maps - it just no longer decides what is SAFE. Monsters below are not counted at all, which lets a mastered bot judge a map by what it actually earns there (see ).
member.param: The lowest monster level worth counting.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.IsPermanentMonsterSpawn(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.MonsterSpawnArea)
member.summary: Whether the spawn area holds monsters which actually stand on the map at all times. The event spawns (golden monsters, the invasion and wave areas) are configured on the regular maps too, but only exist while their event runs - a bot judging a map by them would travel to hunting grounds which are empty most of the day, and would think its current map holds far stronger monsters than it can find there. Same class of mistake as walking to a merchant that is only spawned now and then, see .

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryPickEasierMap(MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.WarpInfo@,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Picks the legally warpable map with the strongest monsters the bot can safely fight among those EASIER than where it stands now - one step down, not a retreat to the starter map. Used when the current map pays nothing (see ): the bot keeps stepping down every barren stretch until it finds ground it can actually farm, and the regular map choice carries it back up as its gear and level recover.
member.param: The warp info of the chosen map.
The level of the strongest safe monster there.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryPickBetterMap(System.Boolean,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.WarpInfo@,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Picks the legally warpable map (other than the current one) that offers the strongest monsters the bot can still safely handle if it is meaningfully better than the current map, with its warp gate. In escape mode (fleeing a hostile or illegal map) any legal map with something safe to hunt counts, no matter how it compares to the current one.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryPickBetterMapCore(System.Boolean,System.Int32,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.WarpInfo@,MUnique.OpenMU.DataModel.Configuration.GameMapDefinition@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Picks the best map (see ), counting only monsters of at least .

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.TryPickHuntingGround(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.GameMap,MUnique.OpenMU.Pathfinding.Point@,System.Int32@)
member.summary: Picks a hunting ground point from the map's monster spawn areas, preferring the strongest monsters the bot can safely fight (see ) - best experience without being slaughtered. If nothing on the map is safe, it falls back to the weakest monsters available (the bot should warp away anyway).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotNavigator.ManhattanTravelHeuristic
member.summary: A Manhattan distance heuristic (the pathfinder applies its own estimate multiplier), used to turn the otherwise unguided search into A* for long-distance bot travel.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler
member.summary: Lets a server-side bot party up with players who invite it (enabled by ): the invitation is accepted after a short human-like delay, and the bot then follows the leader like any party member (see the follow logic in ). A bot stays in the party with its human companion for as long as the party exists and the companion is reachable - a player who groups a bot keeps a companion for the whole session, and the bot only leaves on the engine's own terms: the party disbands, it is kicked, it can no longer legally follow the leader to another map, every human companion has been disconnected without reconnecting for longer than the grace period, or before its own logout, as when the presence rotation or a fault restart stops it. Safeguards keep it believable: no acceptance while the bot is on an errand (shopping trip) or has unfinished business (revenge), and the invitation is re-validated when the delay has passed - the inviter may have joined another party or left. There is no level gate, matching OpenMU's own party action: it is the player who invites.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.MinAcceptDelay
member.summary: Lower bound of the human-like delay before the bot answers an invitation.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.MaxAcceptDelay
member.summary: Upper bound of the human-like delay before the bot answers an invitation.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.PartyDisconnectGracePeriod
member.summary: How long a bot waits in a dead party before leaving (grace for reconnect/off-level).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.TryScheduleAcceptAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player,System.Nullable{System.TimeSpan})
member.summary: Schedules the acceptance of a party invitation to a bot, if the bot is available for it. Called from the auto-accept criteria of .
member.param: The invited player; only server-side bots schedule an accept.
The player who sent the party request.
Overrides the human-like random delay (used by tests).
member.returns: True, if the invitation was taken and will be answered; false, if no criteria matched.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.ProcessAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer,System.Nullable{System.DateTime})
member.summary: Drives the bot's party behavior; called from the bot's regular evaluation tick. Answers a pending invitation once its delay passed, and walks the bot out of a dead party once the disconnect grace period has elapsed.
member.param: Overrides the current time used for the grace-period check (used by tests).

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.HasHumanCompanion(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Player)
member.summary: Determines whether the bot's party contains a human player (any live member which is not a server-side ).
member.returns: True, if a human player is in the bot's party.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPartyHandler.LeaveBotPartyAsync(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Offline.OfflinePlayer)
member.summary: Lets the bot leave the bot-only party it hunts in, so it can join the player who invited it: a living player takes precedence over the bot's own company. When the bot LEADS that party, the group is broken up instead - the engine does not hand the mastership over to another member when the master leaves (it only removes them from the member list), which would leave the remaining bots following a leader who is not in their party anymore. Their next hourly re-formation groups them again (see ).

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer
member.summary: A connection-less bot player. It reuses the whole offline-player intelligence (combat, buffs, healing, pickup) and adds a which makes it roam to level-appropriate hunting grounds instead of standing on a fixed spawn position.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer.ConsecutiveFailuresUntilRestart
member.summary: After this many AI ticks failing in a row, the bot is considered broken and gets restarted. The engine's attribute system is not thread-safe, and a lost race can corrupt a character's attribute graph for good: every following tick throws, the bot stops playing and floods the log with the same exception until the server restarts. A fresh login rebuilds the graph and heals it, which is exactly what a player would do. The threshold is high enough that a single failing tick (a transient race, a monster which just died) is simply skipped, like before.

member.name: M:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer.#ctor(MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.IGameContext)
member.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer.AwaitsMasterRestart
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this bot evolved into its master class and still needs the "relog" which mounts the master attributes (see ). Set from the bot's own tick, where the evolution runs; acted upon by the maintenance pass, which is the only place allowed to restart a bot (a restart from within the bot's own timer callback would tear down the very loop it runs in).

member.name: P:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotPlayer.AwaitsFaultRestart
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this bot's AI keeps failing and it has to be restarted (see ). Acted upon by the maintenance pass, which is the only place allowed to restart a bot.

member.name: T:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression
member.summary: The shared progression rules of server-side bots: how a bot of a given class invests its stat points, and which skills it may learn. Used by the when a bot is created and by the when it levels up during play, so a freshly generated bot and one that grew to the same level in-game end up with the same build.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.ClassEvolutionLevel
member.summary: The character level at which a bot changes into its second-generation class (e.g. Dark Knight to Blade Knight), the way a player completes the class-change quest. The quest itself boils down to exactly this assignment (see QuestCompletionAction), so bots take the direct route.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.SkillOrbItemGroup
member.summary: The item group of skill orbs.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.SkillScrollItemGroup
member.summary: The item group of skill scrolls and parchments.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.DarkWizardNumber
member.summary: The character class numbers from the game's data model (CharacterClassNumber lives in the initialization assembly which GameLogic does not reference, so the relevant values are mirrored here).

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.EvolvableClassNumbers
member.summary: The base classes which evolve into a second-generation class at : Dark Wizard, Dark Knight, Fairy Elf and Summoner. The Magic Gladiator, Dark Lord and Rage Fighter have no second generation - their next class is the level-400 master evolution, out of bot scope.

member.name: F:MUnique.OpenMU.GameLogic.Bots.BotProgression.ExcludedBuffSkillNumbers
